tab:reference-year-counts.caption: Annual record counts in the October 2026 oncology reference corpus and registered observation views.
notes: The complete query-matched corpus contains 163,616 unique records. The 15,000-record annual cap applies only to the 2010--2016 feature/history window and binds in 2014--2016. API denotes application programming interface. The API-order view retains the first 15,000 eligible records returned per capped year, whereas each random view samples uniformly without replacement to match the same annual count. All outcome calculations, including training-label windows overlapping 2012--2016, use the unthinned full-reference corpus.

tab:common-membership.caption: Annual full-reference and common-ID cohort sizes, positive counts, and uptake cutoffs in the October 2026 reference corpus.
notes: Count cells report total candidate fronts / positive labels. Common-ID membership intersects candidate eligibility (and, for the raw-first cohort, view-specific raw-first status) across all twelve views within each training year (2011--2015) and the 2016 test year prior to model fitting and calibration. A single full-reference DF20 adjacent cutoff is computed per year and applied across all views. Because 2014 and 2015 training labels require outcome observations through 2017 and 2018, the forecasting split is retrospective.

tab:frozen-history-counts.caption: Raw and processed-graph observation histories of all 2016 adjacent-entry fronts in the June oncology corpus.
notes: The four raw-history columns partition all 2016 adjacent-entry candidates prior to filtering for available DF20 outcome labels. Each gap category counts full absent calendar years since the most recent prior raw occurrence (since 2010). The final column reports total graph-first entries followed (after the slash) by the number of those graph-first entries that had prior raw occurrences. Raw observations reflect check-tag-filtered MeSH lists prior to annual document-frequency (DF), vocabulary, and per-paper graph limits.

tab:df-membership.caption: Candidate eligibility, turnover relative to DF20, and original-label availability across the 2016 DF conditions in the frozen corpus.
notes: Enter and Exit counts are defined relative to the 2016 DF20 adjacent-entry candidate set. Outcome labels are inherited from the original DF20 adjacent cohort, and candidates without an original DF20 label are excluded rather than coded as negative. These unintersected candidate counts precede the three-threshold common-ID intersection used in the matched forecasting analysis (26,489 adjacent fronts and 7,828 raw-first pairs).

tab:surrogate-axioms.caption: Historical document-surrogate pass fractions under full and dated comparison pools.
notes: Evaluations use 100 focal oncology papers from 2016 embedded with BGE-M3. The Mean column averages the six executable document-level probes (A1--A3 and A7--A9). Probe A4 is ineligible in a single-specialty corpus, and A5--A6 require citation subsets absent from the retained schema. Here, RND denotes our rank-noise control rather than Relative Neighbor Density in the cited benchmark, and the remaining row labels identify implemented document-harness scores. All values reflect the originally implemented probe protocol rather than a rerun of the revised benchmark. Native A10 component-response results are reported separately in Table~\ref{tab:component-response}.

tab:component-response.caption: Native component response under three attribution criteria.
notes: Evaluated on the June oncology corpus at the 2016 boundary across three SGNS seeds. For each seed, the pair probe and random-vector relabel branch use 100 draws, while the near-self relabel branch and drift probe sample up to 100 surviving concepts without replacement. The relabel rate sums near-self and random-vector successes over a denominator of 200, whereas the pair and drift rates use a denominator of 100. All three rows evaluate the exact same saved embeddings and perturbation draws, with strict and dominance rules modifying the near-self relabel and drift criteria while leaving the random-vector branch and pair probe unchanged. The final column reports the three-seed mean and population SD (divisor three) of the row mean. The historical component-level pass threshold is 0.8, and these native rates are excluded from the document-surrogate mean.

tab:rc-adjacent.caption: Pair-only recombination comparisons for the adjacent DF20 cohort in the frozen corpus.
notes: $S$ denotes the 39-column ordered B2+B7 structural baseline, $P$ prior cosine proximity, $Z=\log(\deg_t(u)\deg_t(v)+1)$, and $R$ the fitted residualized prior distance. Both training and evaluation are restricted to the specified pair and proximity subpopulation, with missing $P$ and $R$ values retained as NaN in the all-pair analyses. Brackets report the 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles across 2,000 shared-concept multiplier draws conditional on the fitted models and realized corpus.

notes: Adjacent excl. and Raw-first excl. report the number of view-eligible 2016 fronts removed by the respective twelve-view common-ID mask. tab:view-contrasts.caption: Paired difference-in-increment contrasts ($\Delta\Delta$) between observation views in the October reference corpus.
notes: All contrasts reuse the 2,000 globally shared concept-multiplier draws. Random-mean contrasts average the ten realized random document views within each model seed before taking differences. View-specific contrasts reflect both feature and candidate-set changes, whereas common-ID contrasts hold training and test front IDs and outcome labels fixed across views. All twelve conditional intervals span zero, establishing neither systematic API-order inflation nor formal equivalence across observation views.

tab:random-dispersion.caption: Dispersion across the ten realized random document views.
notes: Each view-level observation is the ten-model-seed mean for one realized random document view. Across-view SDs use a sample divisor of nine and quantify dispersion across document subsamples separately from within-view model-seed SDs and conditional multiplier bounds. The ten views by ten model seeds represent subsamples and model initializations on a single reference snapshot rather than 100 independent datasets.

tab:full-history.caption: Omitted prior full-reference occurrences among 2016 pairs classified as raw-first within each observation view.
notes: This outcome-free audit checks whether each 2016 pair classified as raw-first within a given view had an earlier retained raw co-occurrence in the complete reference corpus between 2010 and 2015. Columns In 2015, In 2014, and Earlier partition omitted prior occurrences by their most recent full-reference year (with Earlier covering 2010--2013). No forecasting models or outcome labels enter this audit. For Random 2 and Random 5, denominators count raw-first pairs only (12,650 and 12,680), excluding the single raw-first term present in each view's mixed-front forecasting cohort.

tab:generic-baselines.caption: Historical individual-feature performance on the generic adjacent-front population.
notes: Models train on the 2011--2020 cohorts and evaluate on the 2021 test cohort (1,394,464 adjacent fronts and 143,894 positives, with 2022--2024 outcomes) across three seeds. Seed SD uses the historical population divisor of three, and ECE denotes expected calibration error from the saved historical outputs. The TSND feature block comprises front type, LE, RC, prior proximity, native degree, and introducing-paper count, with NS excluded.

tab:historical-controls.caption: Historical robustness, feature ablations, and stronger structural controls.
notes: All rows evaluate adjacent-entry cohorts across three seeds. The first three blocks specify the domain and structural baseline to which the TSND feature block is added. The 2013--2016 oncology rolling-origin rows use the B2+B7 baseline, training on cohorts from 2011 through $t-1$ with a three-year outcome horizon. The remove-LE, remove-RC+$P$, and frequency-anchor rows likewise augment the 2016 oncology B2+B7 baseline, while the 2021 oncology row reports the indexing-lag sensitivity check. Reported $\Delta$ values are three-seed means of paired AP differences (matching differences between unrounded mean APs). Relative to the full 2016 three-seed augmented oncology model (AP $0.446083$), dropping LE changes mean AP by $-0.001974$, dropping both RC and $P$ changes mean AP by $-0.018098$, and replacing neighborhood-stability anchors with frequency anchors changes mean AP by $+0.000368$.
